conventions.convention: Asymptotic linearity uses a centered, square-integrable estimator influence function and a remainder that becomes negligible after multiplication by √n; it alone does not imply regularity.
Allowed DQM paths are one-sided, with t ≥ 0, a common sigma-finite dominator and supplied density versions. Their tangent space is the closed real linear span of allowed scores.

LAN uses mean-one absolutely continuous proxies that approximate actual local laws in event-supremum total variation; it does not require actual local laws to be absolutely continuous with respect to the base law.
Functional regularity requires one common limit after subtracting the actual local target shift, for every fixed local direction. In the finite-dimensional lemma, that shift converges to Dh.

The general-estimator bound assumes open finite-dimensional QMD submodels, nonsingular score information, a dense union of score spans, a common regular limit and finite covariance of that limit. The zero tangent space is treated separately.
Gaussian output covariances may be singular. AC is assumed for the probability suppliers; Countable Choice is explicitly carried for the Hilbert projection and canonical-gradient branch.
The sample-mean example permits precisely bounded mean-zero score tilts, rather than claiming regularity on every possible DQM path through a finite-variance law.

load_bearing.statement: Assume AC. For a common-dominated one-sided DQM path with score s, I = P[s²], and each fixed h ≥ 0, its normalized base-support product proxy L_n satisfies total-variation approximation to P_(h/√n)^⊗n, log L_n = hΔ_n − h²I/2 + o_P(1), and Δ_n ⇒ N(0,I). For h = 0 take L_n = 1.

Assume AC and finite d,k ≥ 1. In a LAN experiment with positive-definite information K, local target shifts √n(ψ_(n,h) − ψ_(n,0)) → Dh, and one common regular limit W under every fixed local direction, there is a probability law ν such that the law of W is N_k(0,DK^−1Dᵀ) * ν. No finite-moment hypothesis on W or ν is needed.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. For iid observations with law P, an estimator asymptotically linear at P with influence function φ ∈ L²₀(P)^k satisfies √n{ψ̂_n − ψ(P)} ⇒ N_k(0,P[φφᵀ]). The covariance may be singular; local regularity and efficiency attainment are not asserted.

Assume AC and Countable Choice. For a pathwise differentiable functional with canonical gradient φ_can, an asymptotically linear estimator satisfying the stated common-limit regularity on every allowed one-sided DQM path has an influence function φ representing the derivative, with φ ∈ φ_can + (T⊥)^k and P[φφᵀ] − V_can = P[(φ − φ_can)(φ − φ_can)ᵀ] ⪰ 0.

seams_checked.note: Opened the supplier page and the asymptotic-linearity, pathwise-differentiability and representer items. Consumers preserve the distinction between estimator influence functions and derivative representers, use the closed score span, establish representer equality from regularity, and carry the projection choice assumptions. The supplier page makes no attainment claim, and the consuming page preserves that limitation.

Opened the supplier page, LAN and regularity definitions, third lemma, and QMD-to-LAN theorem. Consumers use mean-one proxies with actual-law total-variation approximation, justify the joint likelihood limit before applying the third lemma, and explicitly adapt identity-target regularity to functional target shifts. The general bound retains open QMD submodels and nonsingular information; the one-sided lemma claims only fixed nonnegative local directions.
